about: Conformance cases for the record tier (SPEC.md in this folder): a strict JSON reader, canonical JSON, sha256 bindings, Ed25519, the receipts ledger with its head record, frag open and workgraph open with its store. Every expect was written by running the case through the Node packages named in oracle; nothing in this file was typed by hand. canonical: canonicalize(JSON.parse(text)) is expect.canonical, and its UTF-8 bytes hash to expect.sha256. strict: the reader (engine: nesting limit 256; workgraph: 64) reads text (or base64 bytes, decoded first), named file, and either accepts it (its value written canonically is expect.canonical) or refuses it at expect.refused.where (null: no place is named), in the words expect.refused.message. hashes: rule names what is hashed (SPEC.md); source names an object inside a fixture ({ fixture, file, line? }, line counted from 0) or a folder. ed25519: raw cases verify signature (base64, read as Node reads base64) over message_hex under public_key; the other kinds take the object at source, put signature and public_key in place of its own, and run the format's own check (issuer: the key a frag must be signed by); message_sha256 is the sha256 of the bytes that kind signs. ledger, frag, workgraph: the fixture's files with change applied (null removes a file; { replace: [a, b] } swaps the first a for b) are written to an empty folder, argv is run there, and the command gives expect.exit, its answering stream (expect.stream) begins with expect.head, and its whole stdout and stderr are expect.stdout and expect.stderr; expect.threw means the Node tool stopped with an exception and printed no verdict line (only the exit is compared). keys are test keys made from the seeds shown. check.mjs and check.py run each part an implementation offers.

oracle.about: The build that answered every case: each package's version, the pin rule over its TypeScript sources (src/) and over the JavaScript that ran (dist/**/*.js), the sha256 of the generator and of the runner whose adapters it calls, and the Node.js and OpenSSL it ran on. No commit names it: these hashes do. dist is what answered; src is the tree beside it when the file was written, which can be newer than dist (compiling src afresh and comparing with dist is the check).

runner.note: the generator calls the packages through its adapters (nodeImpl)

oracle.rule: sha256 over the text formed by one line "<sha256 of the file>  <path>\n" per file, sorted by path, with paths relative to the folder named and written with /
